message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a project & zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional script to install GPU drivers
```

### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a small `startup.sh` script that installs the GPU drivers at boot:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# startup.sh – run on first boot
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r)
wget https://dl.nvidia.com/tesla/driver/nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run
chmod +x nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run
sudo ./nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run --silent
```

Upload this script to your bucket or embed it directly in the metadata field if you prefer.

> **Tip:**  
> *If you’re using a custom image that already contains the GPU driver, skip the driver‑install step.*

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine REST endpoint directly, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r)\nwget https://dl.nvidia.com/tesla/driver/nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run\nchmod +x nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run\n./nvidia-driver-535.54.03.run --silent"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Send this payload via a `POST` request to:

```
https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances
```

Make sure you have an OAuth 2.0 bearer token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Project ID (`my-gcp-project`) |
| ✅ | Zone (`us-central1-a`) |
| ✅ | Machine type (`n1-standard-8` – change if you need more CPU/RAM) |
| ✅ | GPU type (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`) |
| ✅ | Image family (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | Boot disk size/type (`100GB`, `pd-balanced`) |
| ✅ | Driver installation (via `startup-script` or pre‑installed image) |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add additional scopes/network configs as per your workload requirements. Happy computing!
